newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mahdi's flight seen strengthening Sudan opposition.
newsitem.headline: Mahdi's flight seen strengthening Sudan opposition.

text.p: A Sudanese opposition group said on Thursday that the flight of former Sudanese prime minister Sadeq al-Mahdi to Eritrea would strengthen efforts to overthrow the Khartoum government.

Farouq Abu Issa, spokesman of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), an armed coalition which has started attacking Sudan from Eritrea, said in Cairo that Mahdi's departure was a major event which would worry Khartoum.
Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir overthrew Mahdi's democratically elected government in a bloodless coup in 1989.

Mahdi appeared at a news conference in the Eritrean capital Asmara on Wednesday and said he slipped out of Khartoum last Thursday. He said he wanted "a united effort against the regime in Khartoum, with a minimum of bloodshed".

Mahdi, great-grandson of the Sudanese Mahdi who rebelled against Egyptian imperialism in the 1880s, is a towering figure in Sudanese politics as head of the Umma, the largest party, and spiritual leader of the Ansar or Mahdist movement.
Eritrea, which says Sudan's Islamic government is trying to destabilise the region, supports the Sudanese rebels in their campaign against the government.
"After his (Mahdi's) departure, the NDA internal position will be more militant, and the regime has nothing but to face the big battle with the Sudanese people," Issa told Reuters.
"All of us are working to achieve a massive popular uprising to uproot the regime... with whatever arms we possess, from sticks to rockets," he added.
"After the years of pursuit, harassment and threats by the Islamic Front regime in Sudan, his departure is considered a great addition to the Sudanese opposition," Issa said.

"No doubt the Turabi-Bashir regime is scared and disturbed by this big event," he added, referring to Mahdi's brother-in-law the Islamist ideologue Hassan al-Turabi, who has dominated the Khartoum government.
The Sudanese news agency SUNA on Thursday quoted Bashir as saying his government was not frightened by Mahdi's flight.
Bashir said Mahdi's "joining of the so-called opposition would not frighten the revolution and would not affect its adherence to its civilisational orientation (Islamic law)".

Asked whether Mahdi's destination Asmara, where the Sudanese armed opposition is based, was significant, Issa replied: "It might be a coincidence. But his flight to Asmara implies his support to all available means in fighting the regime... including military activity."
A special committee, formed by the NDA to coordinate military acitivity, held its first meeting earlier this month and heavy fighting was reported in eastern areas of Sudan.
